articles.title: WWE Raw results, grades (Oct. 5): Roman Reigns exerts his control; Liv Morgan vs. Becky Lynch ends in double DQ
articles.summary: Roman Reigns returned, while Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch battled for a shot at Stephanie Vaquer's Women's World Title on the "WWE Raw" go-home show as Money in the Bank looms.
articles.body: "WWE Raw" was in St. Louis at the Enterprise Center on this Monday, Oct. 5. The Money in the Bank go-home show was lackluster, to put it bluntly. But it at least gave us some clarity for Saturday's card, with a non-finish in the main event.Finalizing the inevitableEveryone and their dog knew we were getting a Stephanie Vaquer vs. Becky Lynch vs. Liv Morgan triple-threat Women's World Championship match at some point. To get there, we apparently needed a unicorn-esque double DQ in Lynch and Morgan's No. 1 contender match tonight. All three will now collide at Money In the Bank.Plenty of silliness closed out what was expected to be a solid match. The finish ultimately rendered it all moot though, as Vaquer attacked Lynch and Morgan at the same time — after the usual Judgment Day shenanigans.I mean, seriously, this was an egregious usage of interference and referee stupidity. I'm talking Jessika Carr blatantly ignoring Raquel Rodriguez putting Morgan's foot on the ropes. Things of that nature.The Judgment Day get involved but @BeckyLynchWWE SURVIVES 😎 pic.twitter.com/sBuRGeN411— WWE (@WWE) October 6, 2026 To make it all the funnier, Vaquer called out "Raw" general manager Adam Pearce after she ruined the match. He sauntered out from the back, seemingly confused, like he wasn't even watching his own show's main event — one that consisted of the millionth Judgment Day interference he's ignored for what feels like 20 years.Really, everything that happened tonight made Pearce look even worse than he already has throughout this saga. And the "Raw' GM wasn't done either. (More on that later.)A TRIPLE THREAT MATCH AT #MITB!?!? 🙌IT IS OFFICIAL!! @Steph_Vaquer pic.twitter.com/E9z3T4KY4P— WWE (@WWE) October 6, 2026 Monday Night ReturnsIt must be highlighted that any time Roman Reigns isn't on back-to-back episodes of WWE TV, his subsequent appearance is advertised as a "return." That'd be OK if it didn't happen all the time — and if he did more than just talk for less than 20 minutes of a two-and-a-half-hour show. Tonight's "Raw" was a great example of the bait tactic WWE loves these days.The OTC is HERE and so is LA KNIGHT....YEAH!!! 🙌@WWERomanReigns pic.twitter.com/DzBEFVnWKZ— WWE (@WWE) October 6, 2026 That said, Reigns' immediate interaction and promo battle with LA Knight was fantastic. They kept it purely verbal in the ring before their championship match on Saturday. I've completely lost all faith in Knight pulling off the win, so any upset will be even sweeter if he actually does it. (And he should.)But two things are facts: 1) Everything Knight said is true, and, 2) these two men have undeniable chemistry."You're a complainer" 🤯@WWERomanReigns is telling LA Knight OFF! pic.twitter.com/1LE5BmL1XK— WWE (@WWE) October 6, 2026 "You're the most manufactured, corporate puppet, industry plant I've ever seen in my life." 😳@RealLAKnight will NOT back down from the OTC! pic.twitter.com/GS97kf22mO— WWE (@WWE) October 6, 2026 The 946 problemThis angle has become the most "wrestling thing" ever. And if it's all just a roundabout way for WWE to casually sneak Solo Sikoa back into the Bloodline, they will have done that man a massive disservice, given how great he's been by himself or with Knight.SOLO IS BACK 🔥 pic.twitter.com/258Lb4rWKW— WWE (@WWE) October 6, 2026 Reigns oddly wants nothing to do with any of this, and we'll dive into that more later this week in our Uncrowned Horsemen preview for Money in the Bank.But as for Pearce, as previously alluded to, he's allowing 946 to wrestle a match — aka come to work — next week after Jaida Parker literally attempted murder on Jacob Fatu last week.There's no justifying any of this, and WWE isn't trying, which is why it's hilariously just kind of "wrestling being wrestling." But man, is it funny to think about.Ain't NOBODY safe from the 946 😳 pic.twitter.com/1cWc39Awx2— WWE (@WWE) October 6, 2026 👑 Uncrowned Gem of the Night 👑 Speaking of murder attempts, Paul Heyman wants Bronson Reed to end Oba Femi. Permanently. By squishing him. Squishing him with high-impact blows from his body mass at a voluminous rate — otherwise known as a "Tsunami" in wrestling terms.TSUNAMI 🌊@HeymanHustle pic.twitter.com/a9JuEnGTgz— WWE (@WWE) October 6, 2026 This was just great, honestly. And mostly because it was refreshing to see Paul Heyman back doing promo work. The less we see of him, the more appearances like this remind us how great he is. It came after Oba Femi ran through The Vision following their loss tonight to Penta and Je'Von Evans. That's right. The World Tag Team Champions casually lost on a Monday night. I'm not even sure they mentioned the titles during the match.Nonetheless, all this Femi stalling can only last so long, which makes whatever happens this Saturday all the more intriguing. But as of right now, "The Ruler" is treading water and doing nothing of substance."I'm going to PUNISH you" 😲@Obaofwwe is READY for Bronson Reed at #MITB! pic.twitter.com/qKHhNDPxhe— WWE (@WWE) October 6, 2026 OBA FEMI is HERE!! 👏@Obaofwwe pic.twitter.com/vFx7f39bqY— WWE (@WWE) October 6, 2026 I give this "Raw" a crown score of: 5/10 👑WWE Raw full card results and match grades:Women's World Championship No. 1 Contender match: Becky Lynch vs. Liv Morgan ends via double DQ — 👑 3.5/5 👑The Judgment Day (Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh) def. articles.title: CBI raid at Bhagwant Mann’s camp office, FIR against OSD; CM hits back at BJP
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: The CBI has registered an FIR into corruption allegations involving Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann's Officer on Special Duty (OSD) Rajbir
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: The CBI has registered an FIR into corruption allegations involving Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann's Officer on Special Duty (OSD) Rajbir Ghuman and other senior officials, news agency PTI reported.The FIR follows a Punjab and Haryana high court order directing a probe into alleged irregularities in transfers, postings, government policies and tenders.The high court had directed the CBI to register an FIR after noting that material shared by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) prima facie disclosed cognisable offences.The court had also sought a report on the probe within two months.The CBI has now registered the FIR into the allegations involving Ghuman and other senior officers.Govt to challenge CBI probeThe Punjab government has said it will challenge the high court order directing the CBI probe in the Supreme Court.Chief minister Bhagwant Mann rejected the allegations and accused the BJP of using central agencies against political opponents.Reacting to the development, Mann said in a post on social media:“BJP has started preparations for the Punjab elections. A CBI raid was conducted at my camp office. Now, the ED and CBI will be misused in Punjab to defame the Punjab government and me. articles.title: Paramount closes historic Warner Bros. merger to form Skydance | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The deal brings together two major streaming platforms, Paramount+ and HBO Max, along with networks including CBS, CNN, MTV, TBS, Comedy Central, and Food Network.
articles.body:
Paramount announced on Tuesday that it has completed its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery to create a combined company called Skydance.

The deal, which is one of the biggest mergers of all time, brings together two major streaming platforms, Paramount+ and HBO Max, along with networks including CBS, CNN, MTV, TBS, Comedy Central, and Food Network. Skydance will also gain control of major franchises such as “The Lord of the Rings,” “Game of Thrones,” the DC Universe, and “Yellowstone.”

The merger puts one of the world’s largest entertainment studios under the control of David Ellison. Just last year, Ellison completed his merger of Skydance Media with Paramount, and is rapidly increasing his influence in Hollywood.

The Ellison family is Skydance’s largest shareholder, backed by the billions of Larry Ellison, David Ellison’s father and co-founder of Oracle.

The completion of the deal comes after settlements with a coalition of U.S. states and a Hollywood writers’ union cleared the main legal hurdles facing the merger.

Paramount announced in February that it would acquire Warner Bros. following a bidding battle with Netflix , which had previously reached an agreement to purchase Warner Bros.’ film and television studios and streaming business, excluding its cable networks.

Paramount had sweetened its bid by promising shareholders additional cash if the deal failed to close by a specified deadline and agreeing to cover the breakup fee Warner Bros. would owe Netflix for ending its existing agreement.

“Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry,” Ellison said in a statement. “From the start, our ambition was to bring these two storied studios together and create a stronger competitor, with the talent, resources, and reach to tell great stories in every genre, on every platform, for audiences everywhere. Our focus now turns to the future: building a company that empowers creatives, entertains audiences and rewards shareholders. We couldn’t be more excited to get to work.”

The new combined Skydance corporation will have annual revenue of nearly $70 billion, the company says.

Skydance Class B shares will begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange today under the ticker symbol “SKYD.”

articles.title: Netflix expands TV game lineup with Conjuring spinoff
articles.summary: Netflix just announced The Conjuring: Unspoken, a new horror game set in The Conjuring universe that you can play with your phone as a controller, and it will launch exclusively on the service on October 13th.
articles.body: Netflix just announced The Conjuring: Unspoken, a new horror game set in The Conjuring universe that you can play with your phone as a controller, and it will launch exclusively on the service on October 13th. Here’s Netflix’s description of the game: > The Conjuring: Unspoken is an interactive paranormal investigation you can play from your couch. It’s a narrative experience, so you shape the story by choosing different dialogue options as you play. Using your phone, you scour the historic Red Lion Inn (reportedly a haunted place in England) for clues about things that go bump in the night. > As demonologist Francesca Noakes, you scan the area around you with an electromagnetic field reader, an infrared camera, and a spirit box — ghost-hunter tools of the trade for finding apparitions in the wild. The big screen shows your virtual environment, while the one in your hand serves as the controller for these tools. The infrared camera, for instance, allows you to see a thermal overlay of the environment while you’re looking for cold spots that indicate an otherworldly presence. Netflix says you don’t need to have seen the Conjuring movies to play the game, but adds that there are “a few familiar faces that pop up in the game, and knowing the backstory adds to the overall impact.” The Conjuring: Unspoken was developed by Supermassive Games, known for other narrative horror games like The Quarry and Until Dawn. The studio announced in August that it planned to lay off up to 75 staffers, and Supermassive’s former IT and facilities director said yesterday on LinkedIn that “more than 70” people would be leaving the studio. The new game follows the June launch of another horror title, Unhinged. That game was developed by Night School, the studio behind Oxenfree, but Netflix shut down the studio in August.

articles.title: The hotel TV privacy mistake that can follow you home
articles.summary: Hotel TV privacy risks go beyond forgotten passwords when you sign into Netflix or other streaming apps on shared devices you don't control.
articles.body: You've just arrived at your hotel after a long day of travel. The room looks good, the bed looks comfortable and there's a big TV on the wall with Netflix and your other favorite streaming apps ready to go. So, you grab the remote, sign in and settle in for the evening. Seems harmless, right? Here's the part that's easy to forget. That TV was used by plenty of guests before you, and more will use it after you leave. If you sign into a streaming service and forget to log out, your account could still be accessible after you've checked out and headed home. Before you reach for the remote, here's what to know about hotel TV privacy and the safer ways to stream while you're traveling. Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways AI can help you get better health care. Our free CyberGuy LIVE class Get Better Healthcare with AI has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you prepare for appointments, remember important details, understand complicated medical information, research prescription questions and organize your next steps. No technical experience is needed. Plus, recordings of all our past classes are available, including How to Stop Spam, Phone Security and Financial Protection, each with a free downloadable checklist. Watch the free replays and get your checklists at CyberGuyLive.com TRAVEL MISTAKE PUTS PHONE, LAPTOP AND STREAMING ACCOUNTS AT RISK Why signing into a hotel TV can create a privacy problem A hotel TV isn't your TV at home. It's a shared device that you don't control. When you sign into a streaming service, the app may create and store a session on that television so you don't have to log in every time you turn it on. That doesn't necessarily mean your password is sitting on the TV in plain text. But if the session stays active after you leave, the next person in the room may be able to open the app and use your account. Depending on the streaming service, that could let someone watch shows using your subscription, switch between profiles or see parts of your viewing activity. Netflix itself warns that a TV from a recent hotel stay can remain connected to your account. Its Manage Access and Devices feature lets you review recently active devices and sign them out remotely. There is another wrinkle here. Some newer hotel entertainment systems are designed specifically for guests and offer secure casting from your phone instead of requiring you to enter streaming credentials on the TV. Some of these systems automatically disconnect your device when you check out. That's a much better setup when it's available. Still, you can't assume every hotel TV works that way. What about smart TV tracking? Smart TVs can also collect information about what's being watched. Some television platforms use technology called Automatic Content Recognition (ACR) to identify content displayed on the screen and collect viewing information. The exact tracking depends on the TV, its software and its privacy settings. That doesn't mean every hotel television is tracking you personally or connecting your Netflix identity to everything you watch. Hotel TVs can use specialized commercial software and configurations that work differently from the smart TV sitting in your living room. But it's another reason I wouldn't treat a hotel television like one of my personal devices. FLORIDA SUES NETFLIX, ALLEGES STREAMER TRACKED CHILDREN AFTER PROMISING FAMILIES PRIVACY The smarter way to watch in your hotel room My preference is simple: keep your streaming accounts on devices you control. Your phone, tablet or laptop already has your streaming apps and account information. If you want to watch on the larger hotel screen, first check whether the hotel offers a casting option that lets you connect from your own device without entering your password on the TV. If it doesn't, an HDMI cable can be another option. Connect your laptop to the TV and switch the television to the correct HDMI input. Depending on your phone or tablet, you may also need a compatible USB-C or other video adapter. HDMI carries audio, video and certain control signals between devices, but connecting your laptop this way generally does not give the hotel TV access to the passwords, documents or other personal files stored on your computer. One caution: some hotel TVs have locked inputs or hotel equipment connected to the HDMI ports. If you disconnect anything to use the port, put it back exactly as you found it before you check out. What about hotel Wi-Fi? Hotel Wi-Fi deserves some attention too, although there's an important distinction here. Most major websites and streaming services use HTTPS encryption, which means your password and other information aren't simply sitting out in the open for another hotel guest to read. Still, you're connecting through a network you don't control. A VPN adds another layer of privacy by encrypting the connection between your device and the VPN server. If you use a VPN when traveling, turn it on before connecting to sensitive accounts or doing other private browsing. A VPN service can help reduce what the hotel network or Wi-Fi operator can see about your internet traffic. Just remember that a VPN doesn't make you invisible online. The streaming service you're using still knows you're connected to it. For the best VPN software, see my expert review of the best VPNs for browsing the web privately on your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com. BEFORE YOU CONNECT ANOTHER SMART TV, TABLET OR PHONE, LOCK IT DOWN What to do if you're already signed in If you're reading this from your hotel room and you're signed into Netflix or another streaming service on the TV, there's no reason to panic. Before you leave, open the streaming app and choose Sign Out. Don't assume that closing the app or turning off the TV signs you out. If you've already checked out and can't remember whether you logged out, do this: 1) Check your signed-in devices. Look in your streaming service's account or security settings for recently active devices. Netflix has a Manage Access and Devices section that lets you remotely sign out individual devices. 2) Sign out the hotel TV remotely. If you see a device you don't recognize or one that appears to be the hotel TV, remove it. 3) Review recent account activity. Check profiles and viewing activity for anything you don't recognize. 4) Change your password if you see suspicious activity. Use a strong, unique password for that streaming account. A password manager can help you create and store a long, random password so you don't have to reuse one from another account. If you're changing a Netflix password, keep the Sign out all devices option selected so existing sessions are removed. 5) Check the service's security options. Some streaming accounts use verification codes or other additional checks for certain sign-ins and account changes. Turn on any additional account protection your service provides. Kurt's key takeaways I've stayed in enough hotels to know how tempting it is to drop your bag, turn on the TV and sign straight into Netflix. But I don't like putting my account credentials into a device I don't own, especially when I have other options sitting right in my bag. If the hotel offers secure casting from your phone, that's the first thing I'd look for. Otherwise, I'll use my own laptop or mobile device and connect to the television when possible. I also like using a VPN on hotel Wi-Fi for an added layer of privacy on a network I don't control. And if you do sign directly into that hotel TV, add one thing to your checkout routine: log out before you walk out the door. It takes a few seconds and could save you from discovering days later that somebody else is still enjoying your streaming account. articles.title: Former Hamas hostage counters Hasan Piker’s UT Austin event with her story of survival
articles.summary: Former Hamas hostage Maya Regev spoke at UT Austin on the same night Twitch streamer Hasan Piker addressed the University Democrats on campus.
articles.body: Controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker made waves with his visit to the University of Texas-Austin before he even made it into the Lone Star State. While he was speaking at an event last week hosted by University Democrats, a student group, another speaker with a much different point of view was telling her story of survival. Former Hamas hostage Maya Regev spoke to students with the goal of ensuring that they hear from someone who witnessed the horrors of Oct. 7, 2023, firsthand. In a recent conversation with Fox News Digital, Regev took issue with one of Piker's infamous remarks that "It doesn’t matter if rapes f---ing happened on Oct. 7, like that doesn’t change the dynamic for me." HAMAS USED SEXUAL VIOLENCE 'DELIBERATELY AND SYSTEMATICALLY' ON OCT 7, COMMISSION REPORT FINDS Regev said students concerned about cases like the sexual assault allegations against Cornell fraternity members may be listening to a person who's said "rape doesn't matter." Asked about his controversial remarks about the reported rapes committed by Hamas on Oct. 7, Piker told The New Republic that there was "definitely testimony of sexual violence that had taken place amongst the hostages. But that doesn’t change the dynamic of Israel committing a genocide against the Palestinians, and my opposing that genocide." Regev told Fox News Digital that Chabad, a Jewish organization with representatives across the globe, reached out to her about speaking at UT Austin after Piker's visit to the university was announced. "I'm not here to silence anyone," Regev told Fox News Digital. "I came there to let people hear what I've been through, like the other side of the story, with facts, with pictures, with records." UNIVERSITY EVENT WITH HASAN PIKER IN TEXAS DRAWS BACKLASH FROM BOTH SIDES OF THE AISLE The Anti-Defamation League has criticized Piker for what it calls his "antisemitic conspiracy theories and tropes," and has a list of some of his remarks about Oct. 7, including posting that Hamas hostage and American-Israeli soldier Edan Alexander had volunteered for the "Nazi army." Regev said that while Piker has freedom of speech and "can say whatever he wants," it was important for her to make sure students were getting more than one point of view. Regev also emphasized the fact that she was speaking from her own experience, not things she read about from others. "For me, October 7, it's not a debate, it's not something I read online. It's something that I've lived through, something that will forever be inside me, something that I will have to live with for the rest of my life," Regev told Fox News Digital. "I just think that it's important for them to understand that behind every story there are real human beings." "I was a hostage. I was a Hamas hostage," Regev told Fox News Digital. "I was being held by Hamas, by those monsters, and I think that students might, you know, forget that they are actually real human beings, real families that lost their lives, real women that got raped, men, lives were destroyed on October 7." Regev pushed back on Piker and other online influencers shaping students' opinions without firsthand knowledge. "When they hear an influencer post something, when they read something, it's important for them to check the facts before they are repeating a slogan or celebrating death of innocent people," Regev said. She later added, "I sat with those people. I lived with them for two months, with Hamas people ... I think that people should listen to a person who was really there and not to a person who just sees stuff online and has millions of followers." When asked what influencers like Piker get wrong about the situation in Gaza, she said that they overlook the realities on the ground, particularly Hamas' use of Palestinian civilians as human shields. "Hamas is using children and women and elderly women as a human shield," Regev said. "I think, again, people should know the facts before they're talking, and especially when you're very influencing." HASAN PIKER'S DEFENSE OF HAMAS HAVING 'RIGHT TO RESIST MILITARILY' DRAWS CONDEMNATION FROM HUMAN RIGHTS GROUPS On Oct. 7, 2023, Regev went to the Nova Music Festival with her brother Itay Regev and her friend Omer Shem Tov. When the rocket alerts began sounding at 6:29 a.m., Regev was not so alarmed, explaining, as someone who grew up in Israel, it was something she had experienced several times before that day. "We thought it was just a matter of time before everything will calm down, and we can keep on partying, but after some time we understood that it [was] a lot more serious than what we thought," she said. Regev explained that the group headed towards their cars before being told by police officers to abandon their vehicles and that terrorists had invaded the country. That's when Regev, her brother and Shem Tov began running for what she estimated to be 60 to 90 minutes. They then got a call from Ori Danino, a friend of a friend who was also at the festival. Danino had already gotten out of the danger zone, but decided to turn around and pick up the group to get them to safety. Unfortunately, all of them would be abducted and taken to Gaza. The group drove for about five minutes before "a big pickup truck" with terrorists began shooting at them, hitting Regev in both of her legs. Her brother was also shot. The terrorists dragged Regev, her brother and Shem Tov out of the vehicle before loading them into the pickup truck and driving them into Gaza. While Danino was initially able to escape, he was later caught by another group of terrorists and taken into the Strip. The Regev siblings were released from captivity in late November 2023, within a few days of each other. Regev described her release from Gaza as being bittersweet, feeling grateful to be home while worrying about her friends who were left behind. "It was a total shock. I thought that Omer will return home, like, a few days after me, but then the ceasefire was stopped. So, it was very hard for me. I couldn't believe that I escaped this hell, and they are still there being held, Ori, Omer, all the other hostages," Regev told Fox News Digital. HASAN PIKER CALLS HAMAS 'FAR MORE MODERATE,' DISMISSES TERROR GROUP’S BRUTAL RULE IN GAZA "I felt very guilty that I was saved, that I'm back home with my family. I can get the medical treatment that I needed to receive and there are people there suffering, still hostages suffering, not eating, being abused physically and mentally. But I understood that I have a voice now, and I have to use it, and I'll do anything in my [power] to bring them back home," she added. Danino would survive 11 months in captivity before terrorists executed him, along with Hersh Goldberg-Polin, Eden Yerushalmi, Carmel Gat, Almog Sarusi and Alexander Lobanov. Shem Tov endured 505 days in Hamas captivity and was released on Feb. 22, 2025. With her brother and Shem Tov back home, Regev is finally able to look to the future, something she wasn't mentally ready to do until all of the hostages were returned. Now, she's enjoying the simple things in life, walking outside, looking up at the sky. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "I just want to do everything that makes me happy," Regev told Fox News Digital. "When I was there in captivity, I promised myself that I will live life. I told myself that if I'll ever be home again, I'll live life, and I'll study, and I'll go travel the world, and I'd be with friends and my family. And it's what I'm doing now, you know, I'm just doing whatever makes me happy." "I think that the only thing I wish for myself is to be happy forever and grateful for everything that I have." articles.title: AEW Grand Slam France results, grades: Will Ospreay fends off Kazuchika Okada atop stacked show
articles.summary: AEW made its first-ever stop in Paris for a special Tuesday mega-show, and though no titles changed hands, every match had something to like.
articles.body: AEW Grand Slam France went down on this Tuesday, Oct. 6, as the promotion made its first stop in Paris for a special mega-show. Fans inside Adidas Arena were treated to a loaded lineup of four championship matches. Although no titles changed hands, every match had something to like.Rain StopperWill Ospreay and Kazuchika Okada unsurprisingly shined in one hell of a main event for the AEW World Championship. Both men felt like the champions they are — not only in presentation, but in performance.In the end, Ospreay got the job done with his patented Hidden Blade after surviving two Rainmakers. Okada's greed ultimately cost him when going for a third, which was countered by a short Hidden Blade in tight before the final unpadded blow..@WillOspreay empties the tank to put @rainmakerXokada away and retain the AEW World Title!Watch #AEWGrandSlam France on TBS + HBO Max! pic.twitter.com/f5D4vP3dNm— All Elite Wrestling (@AEW) October 7, 2026 After using the finisher to kick off his title reign, it feels pretty clear what AEW is doing with Ospreay and the Hidden Blade: It's being turned into his version of the One-Winged Angel. What I mean by that is, it's his automatic victory — specifically when he removes the elbow pad to land it. No one has ever kicked out of it, and seeing Ospreay stop a match off that single shot gives off that same feel as Kenny Omega's iconic match-ender, whether or not that truly is the booking intention. So kudos to Ospreay and the booking he's had to reach this point with a finisher.All in all, Ospreay and Okada made some magic tonight, and the International Champion felt like he may actually pull it off. If only he didn't go for that third Rainmaker.The Rainmaker isn’t enough to put @WillOspreay away!Watch #AEWGrandSlam France on TBS + HBO Max! pic.twitter.com/VpNy1ONWpb— All Elite Wrestling (@AEW) October 7, 2026 Next, Ospreay has to worry about Clockwork Carnage at AEW WrestleDream 2026 next Saturday: The new multi-person stipulation match he brought to the company.Coffins and towersBelieve it or not, Darby Allin did not jump off the Eiffel Tower to defend his TNT Title against Kyle Fletcher in Paris. (I know, I'm just as surprised as you are.)This match was immediate chaos, as one can always expect from either man. And it was our lone bloodbath of the night, but only near the end, after Allin was spiked onto the exposed top turnbuckle with a hellacious Brainbuster. A Scorpion Death Lock followed by a pair of Coffin Drops got the job done for Allin, sending Fletcher on his way to challenge The Young Bucks for tag-team gold alongside Kevin Knight at WrestleDream. That's if the Bucks get through The Dogs on Saturday at AEW Grand Slam France, Night 2..@DarbyAllin may be FINISHED 😳Watch #AEWGrandSlam France on TBS + HBO Max! pic.twitter.com/dmZJLr1zlb— All Elite Wrestling (@AEW) October 7, 2026.@kylefletcherpro has the TNT Champion in trouble, and “The Protostar” closes in!Watch #AEWGrandSlam France on TBS + HBO Max! pic.twitter.com/aLrQUu15Bh— All Elite Wrestling (@AEW) October 7, 2026 May the series continueBandido kept the ROH World Title by besting Kofi to start the night. Really, every match we see of Kofi in AEW with a new face just feels so bizarre. The near-20 years in WWE are still rubbing off of the guy.Nonetheless, they put on a fine match that was nothing more than a tablesetter for the final chapter in The New Level's trios title saga with Brodido and "Hangman" Adam Page. Later in the night, it was revealed that New Level and Swerve Strickland will defend against the former champions one more time in a Two-Out-Of-Three Falls match at WrestleDream.Chaos erupts at ringside as @Bandidowrestler puts @TrueKofi away to retain the ROH World Title!Watch #AEWGrandSlam France on TBS + HBO Max! pic.twitter.com/l5h17yDdx1— All Elite Wrestling (@AEW) October 7, 2026 Judging by their last match, this upcoming one should be even more chaotic, and it's safe to say we're headed toward a stronger continuation of the Strickland and Page feud. They couldn't take their eyes off each other ringside. A true rivalry made in Hell.👑 Uncrowned Gem of the Night 👑Anytime a professional wrestling show is in Paris, the crowd is almost always the Uncrowned Gem of the Night. That was true again tonight, as the French faithful got loud just from the graphics shown to start the show. Then there was the start of the main event. My word, what a scene.MY AEW GLORIOUSSSSSS#AEWDynamite pic.twitter.com/H8HlED78QM— Sebas ──★ セバスチャン──★ (@Sebas_Bucks) October 7, 2026 Knowing how French fans typically are, it was no surprise they showed up and showed out again for AEW's first appearance in the country.AEW Grand Slam France was a high-paced showcase of wrestling action that knew only one speed. articles.title: Disney Plus will stream Super Bowl LXI
articles.summary: Disney Plus subscribers will see the same Super Bowl broadcast airing on ESPN and ABC.
articles.body: Next year’s Super Bowl is headed to Disney Plus. On Wednesday, Disney announced that viewers will be able to tune in to Super Bowl LXI on its streaming service when the game kicks off on February 14th, 2027. Disney Plus subscribers in the US will see the same Super Bowl broadcast airing on ESPN and ABC simultaneously, featuring coverage from Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, Lisa Salters, and Laura Rutledge. The streamer will also air the Super Bowl in more than 55 international markets, including Latin America, South Africa, and Australia. This year’s Super Bowl streamed live on NBC’s Peacock, contributing to a boost in subscribers. In the months leading up to Super Bowl LXI, Disney Plus subscribers will also be able to watch two Monday Night Football games. The first game takes place on October 26th between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles, but the second matchup has not yet been announced.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed reportedly called Hasan Piker warning his rhetoric was 'costing' votes
articles.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed allegedly called Hasan Piker to warn that the Twitch streamer's Israel rhetoric was costing him votes in the Michigan Senate race.
articles.body: Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in Michigan, allegedly called far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker and asked him to tone down his rhetoric, according to a CNN article published Wednesday. CNN reporter Edward-Isaac Dovere wrote that although the progressive candidate has denied attempting to modulate his positions ahead of November's election, El-Sayed has avoided discussing hot-button topics such as Israel and American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) funding. Another "concession" Dovere highlighted was El-Sayed distancing himself from Piker despite campaigning with the streamer during the primary election. The CNN reporter revealed that El-Sayed had, in fact, reached out to Piker as his comments regarding Israel caused more controversy. EL-SAYED TRIES TO PUT THE HASAN PIKER DEBATE BEHIND HIM AS MIDTERMS APPROACH "El-Sayed recently called Piker and warned his rhetoric was costing El-Sayed votes, asking him to stop, according to two people El-Sayed told about the conversation," Dovere reported, noting that Piker declined to comment on the issue. El-Sayed has faced backlash for campaigning with Piker, who has a history of making controversial statements such as suggesting America "deserved" 9/11. Though El-Sayed repeatedly said that he did not agree with all of Piker's beliefs, he declined to disavow Piker's comments. FATHER OF 9/11 HERO TODD BEAMER APPEARS IN MICHIGAN SENATE RACE AD TO CONDEMN HASAN PIKER RHETORIC The Michigan Democrat eventually began distancing himself from Piker in August after Piker appeared to blame American Jews for antisemitic attacks based on their support for Israel. "If Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they are singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone is going to come around and take action, not against the state of Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker said during one of his streams. ABDUL EL-SAYED DISMISSES QUESTIONS ABOUT HASAN PIKER TIES ON 'FACE THE NATION,' PIVOTS TO GROCERIES Since then, El-Sayed has said he has no plans to appear with Piker and insisted that his campaign has nothing to do with a "Twitch streamer in California." "The question is not about a relationship I got with a streamer in California. There's not a relationship. The reason I have a conversation with him is the same reason I have a conversation with you. Because I want to talk to the folks out here who I want to have a conversation with. Do you think that you're better off now after two years of [President] Donald Trump?" Abdul said on Fox News' "The Story with Martha MacCallum" on Monday. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed's campaign and Piker for comment.

articles.title: BBC to cut raft of Radio 4 programmes including You and Yours
articles.summary: The corporation said it would be investing in a new consumer programme, while announcing more cuts.
articles.body:
The BBC has announced it will be cutting a raft of Radio 4 programmes including the long-running consumer and social affairs show You and Yours.

The social sciences show Thinking Allowed will also be cut along with arts and ideas programme Free Thinking, as the corporation seeks £500m savings.

Other shows such The Artificial Human and Open Country will also go, it was announced on Thursday, while Radio 5 Live will also see a reduction in commissioning on its schedule and podcasts.

The BBC has committed to investing in a new consumer programme, though, and two new weekly shows exploring ideas shaping the world, and the impact of technology and AI.

Radio 4's flagship history, science and culture show, In Our Time, will expand in length, as will Start the Week and Farming Today.

Director of BBC Sounds Jonathan Wall said they were "reshaping BBC speech audio" in order to "build a strong future for trusted journalism, distinctive storytelling and programmes that bring people together".

"By commissioning fewer programmes overall, we can focus our investment and make our best shows work across broadcast, on demand and different formats," he said in a statement.

"That means accelerating growth on our own digital platforms and reaching more people beyond the BBC, while maintaining the strength of Radio 4 and 5 Live, the country's two biggest speech radio stations."

He added that the "difficult decisions" about cuts to shows and staff were "not based on cost alone", saying: "We need to make significant savings while investing for the future."

Last month, director general Matt Brittin said the BBC's financial situation and changing audience habits "may well mean" some channels and radio stations have to close so resources can be invested in on-demand services.

Brittin told BBC One's Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg that "we wouldn't guarantee any programme or any channel will exist forever".

In June, the BBC announced 550 job cuts in news, nations and TV and radio content as part of its first stage in its plan to save £500m across the corporation over the next two years.

Staff were told of proposals including ending Radio 4's The World Tonight, and reducing the number of permanent presenters on Today from five to four, with a single anchor on Saturdays.

It was revealed that BBC One's Breakfast would no longer be shown on Sunday mornings, and that the production teams making Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg and Newsnight would merge.

It followed April's announcement that the BBC would cut between 1,800 and 2,000 jobs - or almost one in 10 - in an attempt to tackle "significant financial pressures".

Last week, an influential group of MPs said the BBC licence fee should be extended to cover services other than TV, and that the corporation's charter review should be scrapped and made permanent.

In its recommendations, the DCMS committee also said that political appointments to the BBC board should end, to improve public trust.

articles.title: Meta is banning TikTok ads across its platforms
articles.summary: Meta has banned ads from TikTok parent company ByteDance across the US and several other countries.
articles.body: Meta has banned ads from TikTok’s Chinese parent company ByteDance across the US and several other countries as the rivalry between the major social media operators heats up, as reported earlier by Bloomberg. The ban, which went into effect on Thursday, restricts ads and paid marketing messages from ByteDance, along with third-party ads that link to TikTok. “We don’t have to run ads from a competitor whose goal is to pull people off our apps,” Meta spokesperson Christopher Sgro said in a statement to The Verge. “Declining promotional services to a competitor is a normal business practice across industries. We will continue to compete on product quality and user experience.” The move comes just months after Meta agreed to a major child safety settlement, requiring it to pay $17 billion and add new restrictions for teens. Meta has since called on TikTok and YouTube to impose similar safeguards, including by waging an ad campaign that TikTok reportedly declined to share on its platform. TikTok has also stopped allowing users to include links that “open or log you into other social media apps,” according to its support page Though TikTok in the US is now controlled by a joint venture majority-owned by US-based companies, ByteDance remains a major shareholder. In addition to pulling TikTok ads in the US, the policy will also restrict them in Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam.

articles.title: YouTube, Meta, and Twitch won’t say if they’ll allow the US government to livestream an execution
articles.summary: YouTube, Twitch, and Meta aren’t saying whether they’ll allow the US government to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan on their platforms.
articles.body: YouTube, Twitch, Meta, and X aren’t saying whether they’ll allow the US government to livestream an execution on their platforms. The four companies didn’t respond to The Verge’s requests for comment after an unnamed Pentagon official said yesterday that the execution of Nidal Hasan, who was convicted of a mass shooting at a Texas military base in 2009, will be livestreamed. Two platforms responded to The Verge’s inquiries. Jamie Favazza, a spokesperson for TikTok’s US operations, pointed to the platform’s policies banning “shocking and graphic content,” including “the moment of someone’s death.” Kick, a platform known for taking a hands-off approach to content moderation, confirmed that such a livestream would violate its policies. “If this was livestreamed on KICK, it would breach our Community Guidelines,” Kick spokesperson Audrey FitzGerald writes in an emailed statement to The Verge. Hasan is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on December 3rd at 2PM ET. YouTube, Meta, and Twitch’s community guidelines suggest that this type of content wouldn’t be allowed on their platforms, but it’s unclear whether they would make an exception for the US government. Meta, Twitch, and X’s community guidelines explicitly state that violent content involving death isn’t allowed, while YouTube bans content that “encourages dangerous or illegal activities that risk serious physical harm or death.” YouTube says livestreams that “feature someone holding or handling a firearm” aren’t allowed, either. Rumble, an online video platform known for hosting far-right influencers, also didn’t respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: WWE SmackDown results, grades (Oct. 9): New champs crowned on the Money in the Bank go-home show
articles.summary: "WWE SmackDown" headed to Lafayette on Friday night for the Money in the Bank go-home show, where new tag-team champions were crowned.
articles.body: "WWE SmackDown" was in Lafayette, Louisiana on this Friday, Oct. 9, for the go-home show before Money in the Bank in New Orleans. It wasn't the most eventful or impactful go-home show, but at least it felt like one, unlike Monday's "Raw."Tatum Time is now!She did it, gang. After my cries of justice for Tatum Paxley following her Money in the Bank qualifier match defeat, the former NXT star has acquired main roster gold. It may just be Women's Tag Team gold, but it is gold nonetheless.NEW WOMEN'S TAG TEAM CHAMPIONS!!! 🏆What a moment for @AlexaBliss_WWE and @TatumPaxley!! pic.twitter.com/7iWcux41Ds— WWE (@WWE) October 10, 2026 There are a lot of mixed feelings around this whole angle, to be fair. But Paxley's victory alongside Alexa Bliss in dethroning Fatal Influence was objectively a fun time in the ring. If there's any problem, it's that Fatal Influence lost this soon after becoming champions. Only 84 days and not a single defense — so, it feels a bit like a rug pull for this stellar faction spearheaded by the great Jacy Jayne.On the flip side, as I've said in recent weeks, Paxley is her. Her upside is undeniable, and giving her any push this fast is warranted. Plus, there's plenty more story to sink your teeth into with her, Bliss and Charlotte Flair. The latter was originally supposed to be in the match until Jade Cargill and her pals took her out backstage.OH NO 😨@Jade_Cargill, Michin and B-Fab with a brutal ATTACK on Charlotte Flair! pic.twitter.com/wcGRoF0YYS— WWE (@WWE) October 10, 2026 The direction we're headed with the trio of Flair, Bliss and Paxley clearly points to a jealousy angle — somewhat reminiscent of the Bellas turning on Paige. But WWE also has the ability, whenever it so chooses, to bring back the "Freedbird rule."For those unfamiliar, the "Freebird rule" simply means everyone within a trio can be considered the tag-team champions. They all technically hold the two belts between them; they just have to choose which two members compete in their matches. Few times does the "Freebird rule" fit, but when it does — like it would here — it could be great, and something new. Especially when it also works in the direction of Fatal Influence — and The Vision over on "Raw." It literally couldn't be a better time to bring it back for all three groups, especially since Bron Breakker doesn't give a damn about the belt he currently holds.Breakking the rulesAll Money in the Bank participants were under one roof tonight. That included Breakker, who met with WWE's two general managers and Trick Williams to start the night. Adam Pearce set up a match despite tonight's show being under Nick Aldis' watch.What made this hilarious by night's end was that it ended the same way every Vision match ends — something Pearce should be highly aware of. It was a classic, bogus DQ that saw Austin Theory rush the ring and attack Williams out of the blue. Breakker is technically losing matches left and right regularly because his teammates are getting him disqualified. Why is this guy rewarded in any capacity? And why should we ever expect him to win on his own because of that? He seemingly can't, especially against noteworthy opposition.The sad part is that the match was good while it lasted with the unique pairing. Whatever. Both wrestlers in the ring is the rule. But we literally saw this exact same thing weeks ago, when Blake Monroe was originally supposed to have her debut match against Giulia.(It's just now dawning on me that Monroe was also nowhere to be seen tonight, despite finally getting said match and winning last week. Ludicrous work, WWE.)Anyway, what's the point of having a referee who just doesn't do their job? Why couldn't those both have been matches? To protect Danhausen and Giulia? Danhausen maybe, but it's Gunther he was matched with. And Giulia has been relegated to being a glorified jobber, which Danhausen basically is too.OH NO 😨@Gunther_AUT with a horrific sneak attack on Finn Balor! pic.twitter.com/rvDqUL2AGW— WWE (@WWE) October 10, 2026 The whole thing was ultimately a vehicle to get Finn Balor beat down by Gunther and nudge them closer to a match. Maybe in a cage or something. I have no idea. This all just felt off.👑 Uncrowned Gem of the Night 👑Promo work, while nothing groundbreaking, was the star of the night on "SmackDown." articles.body:
What to know about Hurricane Isaias Hurricane Isaias made landfall last night near Destin, Florida, as a Category 2 storm, before weakening to a post-tropical cyclone. Isaias is forecast to continue to weaken as it moves inland this weekend, up through Alabama toward Tennessee, but could still bring gusty winds. Flooding and widespread rain also pose risks in parts of Alabama, Georgia and the Florida Panhandle. Tornadoes are possible in those areas and the Carolinas. Isaias is the first hurricane of an unusually quiet Atlantic season.

articles.title: The techlash has gone Hollywood
articles.summary: Amazon’s Alexa Tablets, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, Gears of War: E-Day, and more in this week’s Installer.
articles.body: Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 147, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you’re new here, welcome, I missed you all, and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.) I’m back from parental leave! Part time, anyway. Thanks to everyone who sent well wishes and tips for managing three kids. I need ’em all. This week, I’ve been reading about McMansions and data centers and sports cards and ICANN, trying to run my life on the Dell XPS Googlebook, testing a new and very purple Kindle, reinventing my whole note-taking system now that Google Docs can handle Markdown files, listening to episode after episode of No Such Thing as a Fish, and watching all of Shrinking between the hours of 1 and 5AM while feeding a baby. I also have for you the new Facebook movie, a tech-related procedural, a couple of great new gadgets, the Star Wars game that is going to destroy my productivity, a terrific book about the AI industry, and much more. Let’s do this. (As always, the best part of Installer is your ideas and tips. What have you been watching / reading / playing / listening to / putting in the air fryer this week? Tell me everything: installer@theverge.com. And if you know someone else who might enjoy Installer, forward it to them and tell them to subscribe here.) The Drop * The Social Reckoning. My hopes were not super high for this movie, and the reaction so far suggests it’s good but a far cry from The Social Network. (Which I just watched recently, and absolutely still rips.) Still, Aaron Sorkin and Jeremy Strong will end up in the annals of Big Tech Movies, and I will not be missing this one. * The Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro. For the first time ever, Amazon decided — and I know this might sound far-fetched — to just build an awesome tablet. And it seems it may have! There’s lots of testing to do, and I’m particularly curious about this high-end model with the fancy screen, but I’m hopeful this is the “iPad but cheaper” we’ve been waiting for. For years. * The AGI Chronicles. However bizarre you think the AI industry is, I promise Kevin Roose’s book will convince you it’s even more so. Roose has been deep inside the AI labs for the last few years, and I think came out with the most important story in AI: how a few executives, and the relationships between them, somehow came to determine the future of everything. * Star Wars: Galactic Racer. It’s a super high-fidelity Star Wars racing game in which you (eventually) get to pilot a podracer. That’s all I needed to hear! Oh, and if you’re a Prime subscriber, you can play it for free on Amazon’s Luna service. * Cupertino. The folks who made The Good Wife made a show about technology, and it is exactly what you think it is. I kind of love it! What I’ve seen so far is pretty thoughtful about some complicated real-life legal stuff in tech and AI, and the procedural setup is frankly a nice break from all these miniseries and four-hour docs. * The Surface Laptop Ultra. Microsoft revealed all the details of its most impressive laptop, and while it’s expensive ($2,600!), it also looks and sounds fantastic. Microsoft is pushing the device’s AI capabilities, but this also looks like the uncompromising MacBook Pro competition a lot of Windows users might want. * Gears of War: E-Day. When it comes to raw, brutal combat, Gears doesn’t miss very often. This one also seems to deliver on story and exploration, which aren’t always the series’ strong points; a lot of people have been waiting for the origin-story title, and I’m thrilled the game pulls it off. * Blockers. Michael Lewis tells the story of Elon Musk and DOGE, and in particular of the government employees who tried to stop them from running roughshod over the federal government. I really enjoyed The Fifth Risk, Lewis’ last book about the government, and I expect to like this one too. Screen share One thing about parental leave is that it involves a lot of time with one hand free. Over the last seven weeks I’ve spent dozens, maybe hundreds of hours on the couch while a tiny potato of a baby sleeps or cries or farts on top of me. So what did I do with all that time? Goofed around on my phone, mostly. Too much Reddit, too much TikTok, mercifully at least a little reading and crosswording. I also redid my entire homescreen, because of course I did, and I figured I’d share. Here’s my current setup: [Image: The phone: iPhone 17. I have no desire to upgrade to the 18… but I find myself hopelessly lusting after a Duo. I must not give in. The wallpaper: Black. I am on an endless quest to make my phone less interesting to look at, and this helps. It also helps make my phone a little less blaring when I’m looking at it in the dark, which I do a lot these days. The apps: Unread, Instapaper, Google Maps, Capacities, Daygame, Flora, Phone, Pocket Casts, Spotify, Camera, Prism, Mimestream, Arc. A few things I want to mention here: * The widgets at the top are Calendars and Acme Weather. Acme is a fabulous weather app, and I love the hourly widget; Calendars is, like, fine. I switch between it and Fantastical all the time. I don’t think I like any calendar app. * The only truly new things on my homescreen are Flora and Prism. Flora is a journaling app currently in TestFlight for Apple devices, and it is fabulous. It’s simple and straightforward, but also pulls in workout data, photos, and more to give a really cool snapshot of your day. Prism is a note-taking app that is as fast as texting yourself but with many more organizational powers. I have spent forever looking for a quick, transient way to jot stuff down and organize it later; Prism might be it. * In case you’re following my endless search for notes apps: I’m back on Capacities, which finally clicked for me. It is a project to get the app fully customized, but it turns out to work exactly like my brain does. * I switched from Readwise Reader to Instapaper because I recently bought a Kobo, and Instapaper is so nicely integrated into the device. I like the whole setup, but also the Boox Palma 3 is coming, so my reading universe might be in for yet another overhaul soon. * Daygame, in the middle there, is a thing I built for myself to manage all the daily games I play — it’s just a page full of links to games, which open in various apps and tabs. I might try and spruce it up and share it more widely. Send games I should include! Before I forget, a few more recommendations from my parental leave: * Good Luck, Have Fun, Don’t Die. Maybe the strangest movie I watched over the last couple of months, and certainly the one that made me think the most about tech and AI and the future we’re heading toward. * Tuner. A movie about a piano tuner who falls into a world of safecracking. Nothing I say about this movie will make it sound compelling, but I promise: It’s great. * Furious. One of the most intense, propulsive crime shows I’ve seen in forever. Could barely put it down. * Footnotes. A really cool (Apple-only) journaling and notes app, with emphasis on taking pictures and video right next to your notes. One of the most uniquely designed mobile apps I’ve ever used. * Podcast Shuffle. I had no idea I needed this app until I tried it. You just press a button, and it randomly plays an episode from whatever podcast or podcasts you’ve selected. I use it for falling asleep, I use it for long drives, I love not having to scroll just to get something playing. Crowdsourced Here’s what the Installer community is into this week. I want to know what you’re into right now as well! Email installer@theverge.com or message me on Signal — @davidpierce.11 — with your recommendations for anything and everything, and we’ll feature some of our favorites here every week. For even more great recommendations, check out the replies to this post on Threads and this post on Bluesky. “Playing StarCraft II since the announcement of a new StarCraft in 2030. Just learned that macOS will drop support of Rosetta 2 in 2028 so no more StarCraft for Mac.” — Christian “I’m going on a 13-hour road trip, once again guided solely by an old-school Garmin dashboard-mounted GPS. (DriveSmart series; I forget what size.) I like that it’s a single-purpose device with no ads, no subscriptions, and that continues to get map updates.” — sringsmuth “The recent Hyperfixed podcast episode about the microwave popcorn button is one of the Verge-iest non Verge podcasts I’ve heard in a long time. A BUTTON IS A PROMISE.” — MrEnthusiasm “I recently finished playing Wolverine on PS5, and I’m blown away by its incredible story and graphics. Insomniac delivered on that unspoken promise of slashing and dashing through bad guys — it feels like a whole new level for the character and for fans of Wolverine.” — Josue “Just saw Other Mommy. It’s like a fun amusement park ride in the form of a campy horror film.” — Kevin “I’m building a shed. The tech angle is learning new things using YouTube, online library books, and some AI reviews of local building code pdfs to check if I missed anything. I’m probably doing it all wrong, but that’s what the fire pit is for.” — Tim “I have fallen headfirst into retro gaming on a Nintendo 3DS XL. The catalog of DS & 3DS games is absolutely massive. Running on native, easily reparable hardware, it’s hard to beat in terms of performance and cost. Ok…back to Picross 3D.” — Jacob “The Ezra Klein interview with the ex-OpenAI guy and the Jon Stewart interview with the other ex-OpenAI guy.” — Chung “I have been listening to World War II by Tom Hanks from the History Channel.” — Michael Signing off You might already know about the HTX Studio YouTube channel, but if you don’t, trust me, you need to check it out. It’s a team of makers and creators from China who are making some of the most innovative tech videos I’ve seen in years. I have watched their video about AirDesk approximately 25 times, and I want that desk more every single time I see it. The channel is a bit over a year old, and I have yet to find an HTX video that isn’t worth the time — even the one about the cow. See you next week!
